name: Mississippi
one: Mississippi gives no single last day to ask; ask as early as you can. Below: how, and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Mississippi, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

No set last day

The Secretary of State does not give a separate last day to ask for a ballot by mail. Your ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, so ask your circuit clerk as early as you can. In-person absentee voting ends at 12 noon on Saturday, October 31, 2026. (official page)

Send it back

Mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and received by the circuit clerk within five business days of the election: by Tuesday, November 10, 2026. (official page)

Mississippi’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Mississippi or in another state? What Mississippi says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes, Mississippi allows absentee voting only for certain reasons, and the reasons for voting by mail are narrower than for voting absentee in person. By mail: you are temporarily living outside your county (the ballot must go to an address outside your city or town); you have a temporary or permanent physical disability that makes voting in person a real hardship or danger; you are the parent, spouse or dependent of such a person who is in the hospital far from home and you will be with them on Election Day; you are 65 or older; or you are in jail and have not been convicted of a crime that takes away the vote. Voters who must work during polling hours or will be out of town vote absentee in person at the circuit clerk's office instead. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Call or write your county circuit clerk's office to ask whether you qualify and to have the Official Application for Absentee Elector's Ballot mailed to you. Fill it out, mark your reason, have it signed by a notary public or other official who can give oaths (a voter with a physical disability may use any witness 18 or older), and mail it back to the circuit clerk. The clerk mails the ballot within one business day, or as soon as ballots are ready; near the election the application and ballot may come together. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Vote absentee in person at your county circuit clerk's office (see early voting below). The clerk checks your registration, address and photo ID and asks your reason. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail the sealed, witnessed envelope to your county circuit clerk. It must be postmarked by November 3 and arrive by November 10, 2026. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Both the application and the ballot envelope must be signed by a notary public or another official who can give oaths, and you mark your ballot in front of that person (in secret) before sealing it and signing the statement on the envelope. A voter with a temporary or permanent physical disability may instead use any witness who is at least 18. Voting absentee in person at the clerk's office needs an accepted photo ID; a student photo ID from a Mississippi college, university, or community or junior college is accepted. (official page)

Track your ballot

Mississippi does not list an online ballot tracker. To check on your absentee ballot, contact your county circuit clerk. (federal guide)

Vote early in person instead

Saturday, September 19, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Absentee voting in person at your county circuit clerk's office: 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday from September 19, 2026, plus 8 a.m. to noon on Saturday, October 24 and Saturday, October 31, 2026. The last chance is noon on Saturday, October 31. You need a reason; students away at school, people away from their county on Election Day, people who must work while the polls are open, people 65 or older and people with disabilities qualify. (official page)

Students

At school in Mississippi, away from home

The Secretary of State's page for college students says you must be registered at your permanent residence, which for most students is either a parent's or guardian's home or the campus dorm or apartment, and you can be registered in only one county. If you keep your registration at home, you vote in your home county's races and must contact your home county's circuit clerk about voting absentee; a student living outside their home county can get a ballot by mail, sent to an address outside their home town. If you register at school, you vote in that county's races. The state says to start early. (official page)

At school in another state, with Mississippi as home

The state's college student page does not speak to students in other states separately. Its rule is the same: register at your permanent residence, in only one place. A Mississippi student at school in another state is living outside their home county, which is one of the reasons for voting by mail; contact your home county's circuit clerk to ask for the application. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters and U.S. citizens overseas can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application; FVAP's guide says a registration must be received by October 24, 2026 (by mail, email or fax), and there is no separate deadline to ask for the ballot. They can get and return the ballot by mail, email or fax. A ballot returned by email or fax must arrive by Election Day; one returned by mail must be postmarked by November 3, 2026 and arrive by the fifth business day after the election. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup. (federal guide)

Mississippi in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Most Mississippi absentee voters vote in person at the circuit clerk's office; only voters 65 or older, voters with a disability (and some of their family), voters temporarily living outside their county, and some jailed voters may vote by mail.
  • The notary or official signature on both the application and the ballot envelope is required for most mail voters; a missing witness signature can keep a ballot from counting.
  • Once you cast an absentee ballot, it is final: you cannot vote again at the polls (you may only cast an affidavit ballot).
  • The receipt deadline (November 10, 2026) is the one on the Secretary of State's page as read on October 21, 2026. Mailing early is safest.
  • Military and overseas voters may register with the Federal Post Card Application up until ten days before the election (2026 Voter Information Guide, source 2).
Where this comes from: 5 pages of Mississippi’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. Voting as a College Student, Mississippi Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. 2026 Mississippi Voter Information Guide, Mississippi Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. Military & Overseas Voter Information, Mississippi Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Mississippi 2026-2027 Voting Assistance Guide (current as of 10/2025), Federal Voting Assistance Program (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Mississippi’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
